quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust before carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks, headlight, and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When may you need less following distance?

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. You need more space when the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy. You need normal distance only when conditions are perfect.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. For larger animals, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury in a crash and protects against weather. Good riding clothes provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how the motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: When stopping behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you. The vehicle could back up, or you may need space to escape from traffic coming behind you.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a lane position where oncoming traffic can see you. Maintain space to take action if needed. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars?

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
As much distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if your front tire locks while braking?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever to let the tire grip the road again. Then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags or fasten them tightly. Piling loads high or on the back can raise the center of gravity and throw off the balance. Always spread the weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle in a traffic lane?

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
Always ride in the center of the lane
Always ride in the left part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: No single lane position works best in all situations. Move your position in the lane based on what the road and traffic conditions require.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it better

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use less pressure on the front brake

questions.explanation: When weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle causes a wind blast, where in the lane should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the center portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to adjust if a wind blast pushes your motorcycle.

questions.question: Where should less experienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you use when passing parked cars?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway
The group is easy to see
The group is less likely to be split up
Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than a spread-out group

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than a spread-out group
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group uses less road space, is easier to see, and stays together better at lights and during passes. But it does not get you to your destination faster.

questions.question: What should you do if your throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times
Do not try to twist the throttle

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times
questions.explanation: If your throttle is stuck, try twisting it back and forth several times. If it stays stuck, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person who is 21 or older is considered legally intoxicated if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is ______ or higher.
questions.explanation: A person who is 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, what percentage are caused by the car driver failing to give the rider the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of all crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver does not yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see farther ahead. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: When entering a highway or taking a curve, a group of motorcycles should ride in:

options.text: The far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate to leave it behind.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, you should stay ______ behind the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Normally, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should ride in:

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The center portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding near the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: To turn, your motorcycle must lean in the right direction. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward.
